newsitem.title: CHINA: China planning reform of pension system.
newsitem.headline: China planning reform of pension system.

text.p: China is planning to overhaul its pension system by trying to increase coverage of the unemployed and boosting the share individuals must pay into their plans, the China Business Times said on Thursday.

The Ministry of Finance would also experiment with a social security tax to help to fill out pension coffers, the newspaper quoted Du Jian, director of the ministry's social security department, as saying.
The reforms would be aimed at expanding coverage of workers in rural enterprises and the unemployed, Du was quoted as telling an international seminar in Beijing.
"The main content (of the reforms)... will be to gradually increase the proportion carried by individuals and to gradually lessen the burden on the state and enterprises," it quoted Du as saying.
Medical insurance would be targeted for reform as well, with individuals expected to pick up a larger chunk of their hospital tabs, Du said.
Funds collected for pensions would be put into special accounts with the ministry, which would use a larger share of them to buy state bonds, he said but gave no further details.
Communist-run China has provided cradle-to-grave care for its people but has wrestled with a way ease the financial burden on the state without sparking social unrest.
